gita-12-1.translation: Arjuna said: Some devotees stay always devoted and worship You. Others worship the imperishable, unseen Absolute. Which of these knows yoga best?
gita-12-1.meaning: Arjuna asks a simple question: is it better to love God in a personal form, or to seek the formless, unseen Truth?
gita-12-1.explanation: Chapter 11 ended with Krishna showing Arjuna his cosmic form and praising loving devotion. Arjuna now opens the chapter on devotion with a practical question. Some seekers worship Krishna as a personal God; others meditate on the formless, imperishable Brahman. Which path is better? The whole of chapter 12 is Krishna's answer, and it ends with a portrait of the devotee he loves most.

gita-12-10.translation: If you are unable even to practise, make working for Me your highest aim. Even by doing actions for My sake, you will reach perfection.
gita-12-10.meaning: If regular practice is too hard, simply do your work as an offering to God; that alone can lead you to perfection.
gita-12-10.explanation: The ladder comes down another step. Not everyone can sit and practise concentration. For them, Krishna offers service: do your ordinary work, but do it for God. Cooking, teaching, building or caring for others becomes worship when done with this intention. Krishna promises that this path, too, leads to perfection.

keywords.meaning: work for Me, service to God

gita-12-11.translation: If you cannot do even this, then take refuge in Me, control yourself, and give up the fruits of all your actions.
gita-12-11.meaning: If even working for God is too hard, just do your best and let go of worrying about the results.
gita-12-11.explanation: This is the last and most accessible step on the ladder. Even someone who cannot think of God while working can practise letting go: do the right thing, then release your grip on how it turns out. This echoes the Gita's famous teaching on action without attachment to results, and shows that it is open to anyone.

keywords.meaning: giving up the fruits of action

gita-12-12.translation: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruits of action is better than meditation, for peace follows immediately from giving them up.
gita-12-12.meaning: Letting go of the results of what you do brings peace right away; that's why Krishna rates it so highly.
gita-12-12.explanation: Krishna sums up the ladder in a surprising way. One might expect meditation to be the highest, but he places giving up the fruits of action above it, because peace follows at once. Whatever else we practise, if we still cling to outcomes we stay anxious. When the clinging goes, calm arrives. The verse links devotion to the Gita's teaching on selfless action.

gita-12-14.translation: Always content, steady in yoga, self-controlled and firm in resolve, with mind and understanding offered to Me, that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.
gita-12-14.meaning: The person God loves is content, disciplined, determined, and has given their heart and mind to him.
gita-12-14.explanation: Verses 13 to 19 paint a portrait of the devotee Krishna holds dear. This verse adds contentment, self-control and firm resolve to the friendliness and compassion of verse 13. The refrain 'he is dear to Me' recurs through the passage, showing that these qualities are not rules to earn love but the natural signs of a heart turned toward God.

gita-12-15.translation: One who does not disturb the world and is not disturbed by the world, who is free from excitement, impatience, fear and anxiety, is dear to Me.
gita-12-15.meaning: God loves the person who upsets no one, isn't easily upset, and stays free of jealousy, fear and anxiety.
gita-12-15.explanation: This verse describes a two-way peace. Such a person causes no distress to others, and others cannot easily throw them off balance. Krishna lists the storms they are free of: sudden elation, impatience or intolerance, fear, and agitation. It is a picture of someone safe to be around and calm within.

keywords.meaning: to be disturbed, to shrink from

gita-12-16.translation: One who expects nothing, is pure and capable, unconcerned and untroubled, and has given up every selfish undertaking, that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.
gita-12-16.meaning: God loves the person who wants nothing in return, stays pure and skilful, and doesn't chase self-centred projects.
gita-12-16.explanation: The portrait continues. 'Expecting nothing' does not mean doing nothing: Krishna also calls this devotee dakṣa, skilful and capable. They act well, but without worry and without schemes driven by personal gain. Being both capable and free from craving is a balance the Gita returns to again and again.

keywords.meaning: one who has given up all (selfish) undertakings

gita-12-17.translation: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has let go of both good and bad outcomes and is full of devotion, is dear to Me.
gita-12-17.meaning: God loves the person who isn't carried away by happiness or hatred, sorrow or craving, and simply stays devoted.
gita-12-17.explanation: Krishna names four powerful pulls: excited joy, hatred, grief and craving. The devotee does not swing between them. 'Letting go of good and bad' means not clinging to pleasant outcomes or fleeing unpleasant ones. What remains in their place is devotion, steady and quiet, and that is what makes this person dear to God.

gita-12-18.translation: Alike toward enemy and friend, alike in honour and insult, alike in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and free from attachment,
gita-12-18.meaning: The devotee treats friend and enemy the same, and stays steady through praise and insult, comfort and hardship.
gita-12-18.explanation: Krishna lists the pairs of opposites that shake most people: friend and foe, honour and dishonour, cold and heat, pleasure and pain. The devotee meets each with the same even mind. This is not coldness; it is freedom from being tossed about. The sentence runs on into the next verse, which completes the description.

gita-12-19.translation: who takes blame and praise alike, speaks little, is content with whatever comes, has no fixed home, is steady in mind and full of devotion, that person is dear to Me.
gita-12-19.meaning: God loves the one who stays the same under praise or blame, is content with whatever life brings, and keeps a steady, devoted mind.
gita-12-19.explanation: The portrait ends here. The devotee is unmoved by criticism or flattery, is quiet rather than talkative, and is satisfied with whatever comes their way. 'Without a home' can mean a wandering monk, but more deeply it means not clinging to any place or possession as one's security. Their only fixed point is a steady, devoted mind.

keywords.meaning: homeless, not attached to a dwelling

gita-12-2.translation: The Lord said: Those who fix their minds on Me, worship Me with constant devotion and are filled with the highest faith, I consider the most perfect in yoga.
gita-12-2.meaning: Krishna answers: those who lovingly keep their mind on him, with deep faith, are the most perfect in yoga.
gita-12-2.explanation: Krishna's first answer favours the path of personal devotion. The key words are 'mind fixed on Me', 'always' and 'supreme faith'. Devotion here is not a ritual done now and then but a steady turning of the whole mind toward God. This verse sets the tone for the chapter: love and faith, kept up every day, are the surest way to union.

gita-12-20.translation: But those who follow this immortal teaching of dharma as I have described it, full of faith and holding Me as the highest, these devotees are exceedingly dear to Me.
gita-12-20.meaning: Krishna closes the chapter: those who live this teaching with faith are more dear to him than anyone.
gita-12-20.explanation: The final verse of the chapter turns the portrait into an invitation. Krishna calls what he has just described an 'immortal dharma', a way of living that leads beyond death. Those who take it up with faith, putting God first, are not just dear to him but 'exceedingly dear'. The chapter that began with a question about methods ends with a promise of love.

gita-12-3.translation: But those who worship the imperishable, which cannot be described, is unseen, everywhere present, beyond thought, unchanging, unmoving and eternal,
gita-12-3.meaning: Krishna turns to those who meditate on the formless Absolute, which no words or thoughts can capture.
gita-12-3.explanation: Here Krishna describes the second kind of seeker from Arjuna's question. Their object of worship is the imperishable Brahman, and Krishna lists its qualities: it cannot be defined, cannot be seen, is present everywhere, cannot be grasped by thought, and never changes. The sentence continues into the next verse, which says what becomes of these seekers.

gita-12-4.translation: restraining all their senses, even-minded everywhere, and delighting in the good of all beings, they too reach Me.
gita-12-4.meaning: People who seek the formless Truth also reach God, if they control their senses, stay balanced, and care for the welfare of everyone.
gita-12-4.explanation: Completing the previous verse, Krishna does not reject the path of the formless. Those who follow it also reach him. But he names what it demands: mastery of the senses, an even mind in every situation, and active joy in the welfare of all beings. The phrase 'delighting in the good of all' shows that even the most inward path must include care for others.

gita-12-5.translation: The struggle is greater for those whose minds cling to the unseen, for the goal of the unseen is hard for embodied beings to reach.
gita-12-5.meaning: The formless path is harder, because people living in bodies find it difficult to love what they cannot see or picture.
gita-12-5.explanation: Krishna explains why he called the devotees of a personal God 'most perfect'. Both paths lead to him, but for people with bodies and senses, an abstract, formless goal is hard to hold on to. The heart finds it easier to love a form it can picture and speak to. This is a gentle, practical teaching: choose the path you can actually walk.

gita-12-6.translation: But those who offer all their actions to Me, hold Me as their highest goal, and worship Me, meditating on Me with single-minded yoga,
gita-12-6.meaning: Krishna describes true devotees: they offer everything they do to God and think of him with undivided attention.
gita-12-6.explanation: This verse begins a two-verse promise. The devotee Krishna has in mind does not withdraw from life; they keep acting, but they hand over every action to God. Their attention is 'without another', meaning nothing competes with God for first place in their heart. The next verse says what Krishna does for such people.

gita-12-7.translation: for those whose minds are absorbed in Me, O Partha, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth.
gita-12-7.meaning: God himself quickly rescues those whose hearts are fixed on him from the endless cycle of birth and death.
gita-12-7.explanation: This is one of the warmest promises in the Gita. Life in the cycle of birth and death is pictured as a vast ocean. Krishna does not only show the way across; he says he personally becomes the rescuer who pulls the devotee out, and does so 'before long'. The condition is simple: a mind that has entered into God.

keywords.meaning: the one who lifts out, the rescuer
the ocean of death and repeated birth

gita-12-8.translation: Fix your mind on Me alone, let your understanding enter into Me. Then you will live in Me from now on; there is no doubt about this.
gita-12-8.meaning: Krishna's direct advice: put your mind and your understanding in God, and you will truly live in him.
gita-12-8.explanation: Having described the ideal, Krishna now speaks directly to Arjuna. He names two things to give: the mind, which feels and wants, and the buddhi, the intellect that decides. When both rest in God, the result is certain: 'you will dwell in Me'. This verse starts a ladder of practices; the following verses offer easier steps for anyone who finds this one too hard.

gita-12-9.translation: If you cannot hold your mind steadily on Me, then seek to reach Me through the yoga of practice, O Dhananjaya.
gita-12-9.meaning: If you can't keep your mind on God yet, don't give up: practise, again and again.
gita-12-9.explanation: Krishna is realistic. Holding the mind steady on God is hard, and he does not shame Arjuna for possibly failing. Instead he offers the next step: abhyāsa, repeated practice. Each time the mind wanders, bring it back. Steady effort, not instant perfection, is what he asks.

keywords.meaning: winner of wealth, a name of Arjuna
